AI_Literacies: Artists who are using vGenAI need more knowledge and resources that can inform the critical use of these tools.
Generative_KI: In this paper, we critically analyze Stable Diffusion (SD), a widely used open-source vGenAI tool, through visual and intersectional analysis.
Prompting: When it came to the visual images, we used a specific prompting strategy to produce a dataset comprising 180 images using SDXL.
By keeping prompts minimal, we aimed to observe the default outputs and hegemonic aesthetics in the imagery.
Bias_Ungleichheit: We demonstrate how imagery produced through SD perpetuates pre-existing power systems such as sexism, racism, heteronormativity, and ableism, and assumes a default individual as white, able-bodied, and masculine-presenting.
Gender: Across various images, gender assignments were automatically applied by SDXL, resulting in aesthetics that excluded feminine or non-binary representations.
Diversitaet: Consequently, unless specifically prompted for diversity, the AI-generated imagery lacks diversity to a significant extent, perpetuating ableist norms by portraying stereotypical bodies with uniform characteristics as the visual standard, based on what we witnessed with the 180 samples gathered for this study.
Feministisch: Our methodological approach draws primarily from feminist Science and Technology Studies (STS) (e.g. Wajcman 2010; D'Ignazio and Klein 2020; Adkins et al. 1999; Lury 2020), intersectional critical theory (Crenshaw 1989; Sharma et al. 2023), and feminist media and visual cultural studies (Evans 1999; Hall 1997).
Fairness: Thus, we structure our recommendations around Davis et al. (2021)'s concept of 'algorithmic reparation' which they propose as 'a foundation for building, evaluating, adjusting, and when necessary, omitting and eradicating machine learning systems' which itself is rooted in intersectional theory and approaches.

analysis.AN_Notes: Interpretative qualitative visual analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from 18 deliberately minimal prompts (poverty/wealth, criminal/law enforcement, immigrant/citizen, worker/executive, ideologies, everyday scenarios), followed by a micro, meso and macro intersectional analysis. Prompting is a research instrument; the recommendation that users be more conscious of the prompts they use is Recommended_Practice without a codable technique, so AN_Prompt_Techniques is None. Language_Culture covers cultural context and Global North hegemony in depictions of food and settings; Physical_Appearance covers body size and conventional attractiveness. Mitigation proposals: better curated training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), and algorithmic reparation, regulation, criminal culpability and diverse development teams (Organisational_Process); all proposed. Studientyp Empirisch rather than Experimentell because the prompt contrasts serve an interpretative analysis without a controlled comparison. The confederate flag is discussed as violent imagery, but Toxicity is not coded because the codebook ties it to language. AN_Task None because the work audits a general image generator without a professional application task.

AN_Bias_Definition.quote: Power systems are essentially beliefs, cultural norms, and practices (Guillaumin 2002) that reinforce certain ideologies, such as heteronormativity, patriarchy, racism, and ableism.
Unlike a simplistic accumulation of distinct oppressions, intersectionality explores how systems of oppression intersect and mutually reinforce one another.

AN_Theory_Reference.quote: Our intersectional approach builds on Sharma et al. (2023)'s analytical framework, which encompasses 3 key lenses of intersectionality: (1) the micro (individual) lens; (2) the meso (institutional) lens; and the macro (power systems) lens.
AN_Theory_Reference.locator: Section 2.2 Intersectional STS framework for analysis of vGenAI

AN_Theory_Reference.theory: Feminist STS and feminist visual cultural studies
AN_Theory_Reference.quote: Our methodological approach draws primarily from feminist Science and Technology Studies (STS) (e.g. Wajcman 2010; D'Ignazio and Klein 2020; Adkins et al. 1999; Lury 2020), intersectional critical theory (Crenshaw 1989; Sharma et al. 2023), and feminist media and visual cultural studies (Evans 1999; Hall 1997).

Thus, we structure our recommendations around Davis et al. (2021)'s concept of 'algorithmic reparation' which they propose as 'a foundation for building, evaluating, adjusting, and when necessary, omitting and eradicating machine learning systems' which itself is rooted in intersectional theory and approaches.

AN_Gender_Understanding.quote: Furthermore, the power systems of gender, sexuality, class, race, and colonialism are present in data that is used to train vGenAI, calling for feminist interventions on pronounced representational concerns in the emerging media ecologies of visual culture (Jääskeläinen 2024; Sun 2024).
Furthermore, non-binary gender representations were absent due to the strong binary gender aesthetics, lighter skin tones were associated with wealth and societal status

Thus, SD inadvertently excludes specific representations of individuals, such as wealthy people of color, economically disadvantaged white individuals, transmasculine/cismasculine feminists, and notably, feminists of color across all genders.

AN_Bias_Axes.quote: The immigrants, again, featured only darker skin tones, whereas the citizens had a wider variety of representation.
These age representations exhibited ageist tendencies by largely excluding both older individuals and younger people, including children.

AN_Harm_Types.quote: An exception to this was the material presented above, in which the privilege (such as wealth or citizenship status) was attributed to the white skin color, and the disadvantage (such as criminality) was connected with darker skin tones.

Perhaps most fundamentally, what our intersectional approach reveals-which would not necessarily be so apparent if we had chosen to focus on, for example, gender or ethnicity alone-is that in many cases the hegemonic representation that is constructed through the SD imagery is a figure who is white, adult, able-bodied, and heteronormative masculine presenting.
Notably, there were no representations of disabilities, such as prosthetics, and a notable absence of individuals with larger or smaller body sizes.

Thus, our results illustrate traces of both digital cultural colonization wherein imagery is transformed to align with hegemonic cultural aesthetics, and cultural appropriation where imagery fails to capture the complexity of cultural contexts and instead presents a reductionist portrayal.

AN_Prompting_Role.quote: Users of vGenAI (such as artists and creators) can also contribute to a more reparative approach by being more conscious of how they are generating images-e.g. what kind of prompts they use, and what kind of aesthetics they pick into the images that are used in their work and further distributed in the society.
